chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, who said:
I heard Abu Abdullah عليه السلام say: Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام used to say:

Indeed, all people are free, except one who acknowledges servitude against himself while he is of sound understanding, whether male slave or bondwoman, and one against whom two witnesses testify to servitude, whether young or old.

key_terms.أَحْرَارٌ: free persons, possessing the legal status of freedom
key_terms.أَقَرَّ: acknowledged or admitted legally against oneself
key_terms.شَاهِدَانِ: two witnesses whose testimony establishes a claim

ai.seo_question: What is the legal basis for presuming a person to be free in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes a legal presumption of freedom for all people unless slavery is proven through a valid self-admission made with understanding or through the testimony of two witnesses. It reflects a juridical principle in matters of status and evidence within Islamic law.
